title: Structure with semantic HTML
learningObjectives: Complete structure with semantic html using the project's existing HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and engineering practices.

understand.concept: Semantic HTML uses elements according to their meaning, such as header, nav, main, section, article, form, and footer. Heading levels should represent content hierarchy, and controls should have associated labels.
understand.whyItMatters: Semantic structure improves accessibility, search understanding, maintainability, and browser behaviour. It provides a strong foundation before styling.
understand.analogy: Semantic HTML is the building frame and room labels that make a page understandable before decoration.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; project requirements and release quality must be verified against the actual implementation and user needs.

explain.narrative: The page uses landmarks and nested headings to communicate its structure.

examples.explanation: The page uses landmarks and nested headings to communicate its structure.
examples.expectedOutput: The example demonstrates a project planning or implementation concept; learners must integrate and test it in their project.

practise.guidedTask: Build the page skeleton from your sitemap. Add headings, landmarks, navigation, and labelled controls before adding CSS.
practise.independentTask: Complete the task in a project repository. Keep the scope explicit, preserve user privacy, test the main workflow, and document evidence and known limitations.
hints: Plan before coding and keep changes focused.
Use semantic HTML and reusable responsive CSS.
Test keyboard access, edge cases, and deployment behaviour.
